You can use local or remote views to update the base tables in the remote data source. In the Update Criteria Tab, View Designer, the Update Criteria tab allows you to control how the changes you make to remote data (updates, deletes, and inserts) are sent back to the remote data source. You can also enable and disable updating for specific fields in the tables and set the [[T0]] update method appropriate to your server.

> **Note:** The local base tables that open automatically when you use a view are not automatically closed when you close a view; you must explicitly close them. This is consistent with the [[T1]] command.

If you want to have the changes you make to the local version of a table sent back to the source table, you need to set the Send [[T0]] Updates option. You must set at least one key field to use this option. If the table you select has a primary key field defined and you have selected it in the Fields tab, the View Designer automatically uses the primary key field for the table as a key field for the view.

When you first open a table in the View Designer, the Update Criteria tab shows which fields in the table are defined as key fields. [[T0]] uses key fields to uniquely identify the update records in remote tables that you have modified locally.

- In the Update Criteria tab, click the key column next to the name of the field.

If you have changed the key fields and want to restore them to the original setting in the source table, choose Reset Key. [[T0]] will check the remote tables and use the key fields from those tables.

You can specify that only certain fields in any given table are updatable. You must have a key field defined for a table in order to make any fields in that table updatable. If fields are not marked as updatable, users can make changes to the field in a form or Browse window, but these changes are not sent to the remote table.
- In the Update Criteria tab, click the updatable ("pencil") column next to the name of the field.

In [[T0]], only a few types of files are treated as text files by the source control software. These include program source code (.prg) files and the project file list (.pjm file). Forms, reports, and other types of files are actually stored as tables of information about their components. For example, a form's .scx file is a table of the controls in that form, plus information about the form itself. Table-type files are used to store information about forms (.scx files), reports (.frx files), menus (.mnx files), labels (.lbx files), and class libraries (.vcx files).

Because these files are stored as [[T1]] tables, source control systems cannot treat them as text files (the source control system treats them as "binary" files). As a result, tools for viewing differences between versions of these files cannot pinpoint the differences, nor can you see a history of changes.

In order to allow you to use source control to view differences in forms, reports, and similar files, [[T2]] creates text representations of them. Then, when you put one of these files under source control, [[T3]] creates a text version of the file, which it maintains automatically as you make changes.
 Text representation of [[T4]] file

To support the capability to generate text representations of table-type files, [[T0]] includes the utility program [[T1]], or you can use a different program that you obtain from another source or write yourself.

- In the Options dialog box, choose the Projects file.
- In the Text generation box, enter the name of the conversion program.
- Choose Set as Default , and then choose [[T0]]

[[T1]] automatically calls the text conversion program whenever you add a form, report, menu, label, or visual class file to a source-controlled project. The utility generates a text file that has the same name as the primary file, but uses "A" as the last letter of the extension. For example, for a form called [[T2]], the utility generates a text file called [[T3]]. When you check in the form (or other file) after changing it, the source control software automatically creates and checks in the text file.

If you specify a text conversion utility when you already have forms, reports, and similar files in your source-controlled project, you must temporarily remove them from the project, and then re-add them with text generation enabled.

- Back up all the files that will be affected: forms, reports, menus, labels, and class libraries.
- Verify that the files aren't already checked out.
- From the Project menu, choose Source Control , and then choose Remove Files from Source Control .
- Select the files to remove from the project, and then choose [[T0]] .
- Enable text generation, following the steps described earlier.
- From the Project menu, choose Source Control, and then choose Add Files to Source Control .
- Select the files to add, and then choose [[T1]] .

As it puts the each file under source control, [[T2]] also creates the corresponding text representation for the file.
